records.reason: Keep. The 211-word golden carries four extra security tangents; reduce to the two key facts and one safe-practice sentence.

rewrite.answer: No. A cryptographic hash is one-way, so a hash of your secret key cannot restore it, and Stellar has no network-level key reset. Ciphertext is recoverable only with its separate key or password, and on-chain it becomes public and permanent; never publish a raw secret key. Use your wallet's documented recovery and backup process and keep recovery material private.
keyFacts: A hash is one-way and cannot be reversed to recover the secret key.
Stellar has no network-level reset or recovery for a lost secret key.
avoid: Saying an on-chain key hash enables recovery.
Advising publishing or sharing a secret key.
rewrite.notes: An accurate mention of the hash(x) signer type (SHA-256 of a separate preimage, public once used) is not the avoided claim.

rot.claim: XLM has no issuer clawback; clawback applies only to issued assets with the issuer's flag set

evidence.quote: The issuer sets up their account to enable clawbacks using the AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED flag ... for any assets issued by that account

records.reason: Survivor of the lost/stolen-funds family. Split the key facts so the no-clawback fact is explicit and absorb the 'cannot inspect or trace' behavior; shrink 205 words.

rewrite.answer: Stellar and SDF cannot reverse a completed transfer or freeze a thief's account. XLM has no issuer clawback; only a verified issuer with clawback enabled may recover an issued asset. If an uncompromised signer still controls the account, replace the compromised signers and move what remains. Preserve transaction hashes, contact the wallet or exchange through official support, and report the theft. Never pay or share keys with a 'recovery agent'.
keyFacts: Stellar and SDF cannot reverse a completed theft or freeze the thief's account.
XLM has no issuer clawback; only a clawback-enabled issuer may recover an issued asset.
Safe steps: secure what remains, preserve hashes, use official support, report the theft.
Paying or sharing keys with a 'recovery agent' is a scam.
avoid: Promising recovery or saying SDF can freeze the thief's account.
Saying every stolen issued token is unrecoverable, or describing clawback as generic reversal.
rewrite.notes: Acknowledge the loss; do not claim to inspect, trace, or reverse anything.
